description: 'Use when editing Atelier French or English locale messages, artwork descriptions or translated page metadata.'

# Internationalization Instructions

Read and apply [i18n](../../.agents/skills/i18n/SKILL.md) before changing locale messages.
It owns bilingual key parity, naming, confirmed content, interpolation and reactive consumers.
Use its [artwork naming map](../../.agents/skills/i18n/references/artwork-naming.md) when resolving gallery keys.

Keep additions, renames and removals aligned in French and English.
Preserve nesting, value types and interpolation names, and search generated artwork key families before removing an entry.
A wording correction does not require an artificial change to an already accurate translation in the other locale.
Do not invent artwork details or physical dimensions to fill an optional field.
Use [content direction](../../.agents/docs/content-direction.md) for editorial voice and [brand context](../../.agents/docs/brand-context.md) when changing identity or factual positioning.

Keep user-facing copy and accessible names in the locale files, including image descriptions, viewer controls and functional labels.
Preserve supplied French artistic subtitles and write natural English rather than copying French syntax.
Inspect Vue I18n syntax before adding `|` or `@` to ordinary copy; intentional plurals and linked messages still need their correct message syntax.
Keep messages as text instead of introducing `v-html` for translated prose.

Parse both files and compare the affected keys and placeholders; fallback output alone does not prove English completeness.
Use [the SEO skill](../../.agents/skills/seo/SKILL.md) when metadata is involved and follow the i18n skill's relevant compilation and UI checks.
